project.name: C-Blosc2
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced the saved MemorySanitizer crash against the ARVO workspace checkout `cb15f1b2904c0c4087bb5422cf18a7091fc5ac82`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `986aabad378ad0d819ddb0b6db7469e95ec21985`. The staged checkout's local git history shows `cb15f1b2904c0c4087bb5422cf18a7091fc5ac82` is an ancestor of both metadata commits, and it already contains the same vulnerable `blosc_d()` negative-`cbytes` branch plus the same fix hunk shown in `patch.diff`. All line anchors below use the staged checkout's exact line map.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

classification.classification_note: The saved MSan sink is a branch on uninitialized pointer `dst` in `ZSTD_checkContinuity()`, but the source bug is earlier in `blosc_d()`: the negative-`cbytes` arm only assigns `nbytes` and zeroes `cbytes` when `token & 0x1` is true, so the token-clear path leaves `nbytes` indeterminate and `cbytes` negative before the common loop epilogue consumes both.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491232 (c-blosc2): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target decompress_chunk_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491232
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's `use-of-uninitialized-value` against the staged ARVO checkout `cb15f1b2904c0c4087bb5422cf18a7091fc5ac82`, and the trace below is anchored to that exact source snapshot rather than the metadata vulnerable commit `986aabad378ad0d819ddb0b6db7469e95ec21985`. The exact 64-byte witness is admitted as a regular-header Blosc chunk because `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` parses `nbytes = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`, the harness confirms `cbytes == size`, and `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` returns success. `initialize_context_decompression()` then reparses the same bytes as `header_flags = 0x80`, `typesize = 2`, `sourcesize = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`, computes `nblocks = 12`, takes the regular-header `bstarts_offset = 16`, and leaves `context->use_dict = 0` on this call. In `serial_blosc()`, block 0 keeps `leftoverblock = 0` and loads `bstarts[0] = 24`, so `blosc_d()` enters the split-stream Zstd path with `nstreams = 2` and `neblock = 0`. For the first stream, the bytes at offset 24 read as `cbytes = -1` and token `0x10`. Because `token & 0x1` is false, vulnerable code skips both `nbytes = neblock` and `cbytes = 0`, yet the common loop epilogue still executes; that rewinds `src` back to offset 28 via `src += cbytes` and makes `_dest` indeterminate via `_dest += nbytes`. The second stream therefore reinterprets bytes `10 00 00 00` as positive `cbytes = 16` and calls `zstd_wrap_decompress()` with uninitialized `_dest` and `maxout = 0`. `ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame()` immediately forwards that uninitialized pointer as `dst` into `ZSTD_checkContinuity()`, and the branch `if (dst != dctx->previousDstEnd)` is the saved MSan sink. The staged patch resolves this exact obligation by moving `nbytes = neblock` and `cbytes = 0` out of the inner `if (token & 0x1)` so every negative-`cbytes` token path defines those loop-bookkeeping variables before the common epilogue runs.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled Blosc chunk header. These statements materialize the outer chunk sizes that the harness later validates and reuses as the decompression input/output sizes.
source.value_from: The exact 64-byte witness in `poc` begins `02 00 80 02 0c 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 40 00 00 00 ...`; bytes 4..15 decode little-endian as `nbytes = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `dst` is the uninitialized output pointer propagated from `blosc_d()`, and this branch is the first observed use of that poisoned value.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/c-blosc2/internal-complibs/zstd-1.4.5/decompress/zstd_decompress_block.c:1414:9` in `ZSTD_checkContinuity`, with stack `ZSTD_checkContinuity -> ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame -> zstd_wrap_decompress -> blosc_d`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The negative-`cbytes` decoding arm initializes `nbytes` and normalizes `cbytes` only when `token & 0x1` is true. When the token-clear path executes, the common loop epilogue still uses `nbytes` and `cbytes`, so `nbytes` is read before initialization and `src` is rewound by the stale negative `cbytes` value.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` moves `nbytes = neblock` and `cbytes = 0` out of the inner `if (token & 0x1)` block, confirming that every negative-token path was supposed to define those bookkeeping variables before the later `src += cbytes; _dest += nbytes; ntbytes += nbytes;` epilogue.

tainted_value_origin.code: int32_t nbytes;                /* number of decompressed bytes in split */
tainted_value_origin.description: Source-grounded origin of the uninitialized scalar that later poisons `_dest`. MemorySanitizer's origin tracking for this sample is invalid (`ORIGIN: invalid (0)`), so the vulnerable local declaration plus the untaken assignments in the negative-`cbytes` arm are the concrete origin evidence.

parser_admitted.description: The outer chunk header is internally consistent for the witness: `header_cbytes == size == 64` and parsed `nbytes == 12` is within bounds, so after the harness's `cbytes == size && nbytes != 0` check it allocates `output` and calls `blosc2_decompress()`.

evidence_limitations: The staged source snapshot is workspace commit `cb15f1b2904c0c4087bb5422cf18a7091fc5ac82`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `986aabad378ad0d819ddb0b6db7469e95ec21985`; however the staged checkout is still vulnerable, reproduces the saved MSan crash, and the staged patch fixes the same `blosc_d()` hunk there.

MemorySanitizer origin tracking reports `ORIGIN: invalid (0)` for this sample, so `allocation_context` is null. The uninitialized-value origin is therefore established source-side from the vulnerable local `nbytes` declaration plus the missing assignments in the negative-`cbytes` path.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled outer header bytes are parsed as `nbytes = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`.

After step 1 and `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` succeed, the harness allocates a 64-byte destination buffer and calls `blosc2_decompress(data, size, output, 64)`. This buffer is the initial base for `_dest` in the later vulnerable block loop.

The decompressor reparses the same witness as `header_flags = 0x80`, `typesize = 2`, `sourcesize = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`. The malformed-header checks at lines 1589-1598 accept these values, so execution continues into the regular chunk-layout setup.

With `sourcesize = 12` and `blocksize = 1`, this computes `context->nblocks = 12` and `context->leftover = 0`. The header takes the regular-header branch, so `bstarts_offset = 16` and `context->bstarts` is the block-start table beginning at byte 16; on this path the `BLOSC2_USEDICT` branch is not taken, so `context->use_dict` stays 0.

On the first loop iteration (`j == 0`), `bsize` starts as `context->blocksize = 1`, and `leftoverblock` stays `0` because only the final block would flip it to `1` when `context->leftover > 0`. This block remains eligible for split-stream decompression.

fine_trace.code: int32_t src_offset = memcpyed ? BLOSC_MAX_OVERHEAD + j * context->blocksize : sw32_(bstarts + j);
fine_trace.note: With `header_flags = 0x80` leaving `memcpyed` clear, the ternary reads the block-start table entry instead of the memcpy fast path. For `j == 0`, bytes 16..19 are `18 00 00 00`, so `src_offset = 24` and block 0 begins at the attacker-controlled length field `ff ff ff ff`.

From `header_flags = 0x80`, this computes `compformat = 4` and `dont_split = 0`. Later in the same function, `compformat == BLOSC_ZSTD_FORMAT` is the only branch that matches, so this block is on the Zstd path and remains eligible for split-stream decoding.

Because `dont_split == 0`, `leftoverblock == 0`, and `context->use_dict == 0`, this block takes the split-stream branch and sets `nstreams = typesize = 2`. With `bsize = 1`, `neblock = 1 / 2 = 0`, so each stream has a zero-byte logical output extent.

At block-0 offset 24, the first stream length is `cbytes = -1`, and the next byte is `token = 0x10`, so `token & 0x1` is false. Vulnerable code therefore exits this negative-`cbytes` arm without executing either `nbytes = neblock` or `cbytes = 0`, leaving `nbytes` indeterminate and `cbytes` still `-1`.

The common loop epilogue still runs. Because `cbytes` remained `-1`, `src += cbytes` moves the pointer back from 29 to 28, and because `nbytes` was never initialized, `_dest += nbytes` and `ntbytes += nbytes` propagate an indeterminate destination pointer and byte count into the next stream iteration.

On the second loop iteration (`j == 1`), the rewound position 28 presents bytes `10 00 00 00`, so this stream parses `cbytes = 16` and advances `src` to payload offset 32. `srcsize` also drops to 16, so the positive-length decompressor call is reached.

Because `compformat == BLOSC_ZSTD_FORMAT`, the positive-length second stream is dispatched to Zstd. `blosc_d()` passes the payload at offset 32, `compressed_length = 16`, the step-10 indeterminate `_dest` as `dst`, and `maxout = neblock = 0` into `zstd_wrap_decompress()`, which forwards the same poisoned `dst` into `ZSTD_decompressDCtx()` and `ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame()`.

Sink. `ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame()` unconditionally calls `ZSTD_checkContinuity(dctx, dst)`, and this branch is the first observed use of the uninitialized `dst` pointer propagated from step 10 through step 12. Stage 01's saved MSan trace reports this exact site.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MemorySanitizer origin tracking is invalid for this sample, but the staged fix diff and steps 9-12 show that the missing negative-`cbytes` bookkeeping assignments in `blosc_d()` are the unique source-level producer of the uninitialized `dst` later branched on in `ZSTD_checkContinuity()`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch moves `nbytes = neblock` and `cbytes = 0` out of the inner `if (token & 0x1)` block, so the token-clear negative-`cbytes` path exercised here no longer leaves `_dest` and `src` bookkeeping undefined before the later Zstd call.

poc.trigger: Exact staged 64-byte witness `020080020c000000010000004000000018000000f5ffffffffffffff10000000180000001000000010000000102e0000f80504fefe00200008ff000000000010`. As a Blosc chunk it yields outer header `nbytes = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, `cbytes = 64`, and first block offset `bstarts[0] = 24`; the first stream there encodes `cbytes = -1` and `token = 0x10`, after which the vulnerable loop rewinds and reuses bytes `10 00 00 00` as second-stream `cbytes = 16`, reaching the saved MSan sink in `ZSTD_checkContinuity()`.

format.name: Blosc chunk
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to this exact 64-byte staged witness (sha256 `9fa0e7811dd94e84f17f8152023b1588f655d0e7cf51bf5b22a0643f8dbc27c5`). It must keep the outer header bytes 4..15 as `nbytes = 12`, `blocksize = 1`, and `cbytes = 64`, the first block-start entry bytes 16..19 as `24`, the first stream length bytes 24..27 as `ff ff ff ff` (`cbytes = -1`), and byte 28 as token `0x10` with bit 0 clear. Those exact values are what make the vulnerable `blosc_d()` leave `nbytes` uninitialized, rewind `src`, reinterpret bytes `10 00 00 00` as the second stream's positive `cbytes = 16`, and call Zstd with uninitialized `dst`. No broader input family is claimed.
